# freshdesk_ticket (Resource)

A support ticket.

-> Tickets are usually created by customers rather than declared in configuration. This resource is most useful for seeding fixtures and for automation that must own a ticket's lifecycle.

~> Deleting this resource moves the ticket to the trash, where Freshdesk keeps it for 30 days before removing it permanently.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "freshdesk_ticket" "onboarding" {
  subject      = "Welcome aboard"
  description  = "<p>Reach out here with any setup questions.</p>"
  requester_id = freshdesk_contact.avery.id
  priority     = 1
  status       = 2
  tags         = ["onboarding"]
}

resource "freshdesk_contact" "avery" {
  name  = "Avery Stone"
  email = "avery@northwind.example"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `description` (String) Opening message of the ticket, in HTML.

~> Freshdesk rewrites the markup it is given, so this attribute keeps what you configured and `description_text` exposes the stored plain-text rendering. A body edited in the portal cannot be detected as drift.
- `subject` (String) Subject line of the ticket.

### Optional

- `cc_emails` (Set of String) Addresses copied on the ticket's correspondence.
- `company_id` (Number) ID of the company the ticket belongs to.
- `custom_fields` (Map of String) Custom field values keyed by field name. Non-string values are given as JSON.
- `due_by` (String) When the ticket must be resolved (RFC 3339).
- `email` (String) Email address of the requester, when no `requester_id` is given.
- `email_config_id` (Number) ID of the email config the ticket is associated with.
- `fr_due_by` (String) When the first response is due (RFC 3339).
- `group_id` (Number) ID of the group the ticket is assigned to. Freshdesk fills this in when an automation routes the ticket.
- `name` (String) Name of the requester, used when creating one.
- `parent_id` (Number) ID of the parent ticket, for a child ticket.
- `phone` (String) Phone number of the requester, when no `requester_id` is given.
- `priority` (Number) Priority: `1` low, `2` medium, `3` high, `4` urgent. Freshdesk requires a priority on every ticket, so this defaults to `1`.
- `product_id` (Number) ID of the product the ticket concerns. Freshdesk fills this in from the email config when it is not given.
- `requester_id` (Number) ID of the contact who raised the ticket. One of `requester_id`, `email`, `phone` or `name` identifies the requester.
- `responder_id` (Number) ID of the agent the ticket is assigned to. Freshdesk fills this in when an automation assigns the ticket.
- `source` (Number) Channel the ticket arrived on: `1` email, `2` portal, `3` phone, `7` chat, `9` feedback widget, `10` outbound email, `11` e-commerce.
- `status` (Number) Status: `2` open, `3` pending, `4` resolved, `5` closed. Accounts may define further custom statuses. Freshdesk requires a status on every ticket, so this defaults to `2`.
- `tags` (Set of String) Tags applied to the ticket.
- `type` (String) Ticket type. The allowed values are the choices configured on the account's Type field.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the ticket was created (RFC 3339).
- `description_text` (String) Plain-text rendering of `description`.
- `id` (String) Numeric identifier of the ticket.
- `is_escalated` (Boolean) Whether the ticket has breached its resolution SLA.
- `spam` (Boolean) Whether the ticket has been marked as spam.
- `updated_at` (String) When the ticket was last changed (RFC 3339).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by numeric ID.
terraform import freshdesk_ticket.example 42
```
